To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
heat transfer between building zones through a water loop can lead to annual energy savings between 7%–27%, depending on climate conditions and occupancy level.
the novel configuration of the active beam system can lead to energy savings between 1.5 and 6.5 kWh/m2 per year depending on climate location and occupancy level.

the heat transfer between zones can lead to annual energy savings in active beam systems, which vary between 7% (in the case of a building located in a warm climate, with a low occupancy level) and 27% (in a building located in an extremely cold climate, with a high occupancy level), in relation to traditional configurations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of climate and occupancy on the heat transfer between zones in a building with the aim to identify the scenarios where the energy saving potential of the novel circuit configuration is maximized.
an innovative configuration that has the potential to reduce energy consumption in buildings.
the influence of climate and occupancy levels on a new concept of building hydronics, which is expected to be a key element in future energy efficient buildings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heat transfer between building zones through a water loop at room temperature can lead to significant energy savings, especially in buildings located in climates with large temperature variations.
the potential for heat transfer in a room-temperature circuit is higher in cold and humid climates and in buildings with a higher occupancy level.
the energy savings potential is higher when the climate is mild.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heat transfer between zones can be used to increase the efficiency of the hydronic circuit in buildings.
a room-temperature loop can provide energy savings of 7–27% in a building, depending on climate and occupancy level, and this is achieved with a simple change in the circuit configuration.
a water loop operating at a constant temperature of 22 ºC can be used to deliver heat from warm zones to cold zones.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy reduction potential of the water-loop configuration is highly sensitive to climate conditions.
the energy savings potential is strongly influenced by the diversity of thermal needs in different zones.

the energy saving potential of the novel circuit is higher for buildings with high diversity of thermal loads, such as in the case of buildings with high occupancy levels and/or buildings located in climates with large differences between winter and summer temperatures.
